messages:
marie (Support): Olga from AcmeHealth reported intermittent partial SSE messages and clients seeing truncated JSON events after ~7s. customer says reconnects are frequent and they get duplicate tokens on reconnects. they attached a short recording of the browser console and a curl trace.

olga (Customer): repro steps: 1) use our web agent behind their corporate gRPC-web gateway -> 2) connect to /v1/stream with h2 upstream but edge translates to h1 via proxy -> 3) after ~6-10s we sometimes get a half-event and then connection closes. If I refresh, the client reconnect tries the same stream id and gets duplicated output.

marie (Support): Thanks — logging the report and escalating to infra. tagging @dinesh and @kai for h2<->h1 translation issues. Any quick mitigation? :eyes:

dinesh (SRE): Seen similar when the intermediary strips `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` or buffers to a full response. Proxy drops at chunk boundary and sends FIN; downstream H1 client sees truncated chunk and closes. Important: our server writes SSE as app/stream+json chunks with `

` separators. If an intermediate merges chunks we get partial JSON parse on client.

kai (Eng-runtime): Two things to check: (1) connection reuse / keepalive timeouts on the gRPC-gateway; (2) whether the proxy rewrites `Content-Length`. Also check our streaming sentinel: we append a newline after every event but if proxy coalesces boundaries, client-side parser should be resilient. Can you paste the curl traces?

olga (Customer): here's the curl from browser env that reproduces: ```curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=llm-test"``` output: ```* Connected to api.redwood.example (10.0.0.2) port 443 (#0)\n> GET /v1/stream?model=llm-test HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.example\n> Accept: text/event-stream\n> \n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n< date: Wed, 15 Mar 2025 14:10:10 GMT\n< content-type: text/event-stream\n< transfer-encoding: chunked\n<\n0003\n{\n* connection #0 to host api.redwood.example left intact\n``` The response cuts in the middle of JSON.

henry (SDK): Also saw clients using fetch() with `ReadableStream` that assume each `

` is a full event; if a chunk boundary cuts JSON it can throw. SDK should buffer until event delimiter. But that doesn't solve the root: proxy trimming chunk boundaries.

dinesh (SRE): Repro on our staging: spin up a small nginx that proxies h2->h1 with `proxy_buffering on; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` then run a tiny server that streams SSE every 1s. With default nginx with certain buffer sizes, it will coalesce and flush only on buffer full or `proxy_set_header Connection '';` weirdness. I can reproduce a split JSON and client parse error.

marie (Support): Customer reports also seeing a billing spike in their tenant metrics because reconnects are counted as fresh sessions — @billing-bot any note?

billing-bot: Noted: customer curious why token/usage jumped 3x during reconnect storm window 2025-03-15T14:08:00Z - 14:13:00Z. We log reconnects as new requests; if they resumed with the same conversation ID they still incur token costs because server replays new tokens. Recommend temporary credit until root cause fixed.

kai (Eng-runtime): Immediate mitigation options: 1) server-side resilience — buffer and not emit event until we have complete JSON boundary; 2) add small idempotency / dedupe token: on reconnect if client sends same stream_id we can detect resumed offset and avoid re-sending tokens already billed; 3) send a streaming heartbeat (special SSE event `event: chunk-boundary`
`data: ok`) every 1s to make sure proxies flush. Option 3 is low-risk and quick.

dinesh (SRE): I agree on heartbeat. Also we should patch our router's `Content-Encoding` passthrough to avoid changing `Transfer-Encoding`. And in the short term, set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx-like mediators.

olga (Customer): Can you push a quick change? client side we can also add a reconnection backoff and resume token, but they prefer server fix.

marie (Support): Next steps: 1) Eng runtime to push heartbeat toggle as feature flag for the tenant; 2) SRE to provide proxy header guidance for customers' gateways and a KB article; 3) Billing to review credits.

kai (Eng-runtime): I'll open a canary flag: `streaming.heartbeat.enable` scoped to AcmeHealth. Will send a canary release to edge in 10 min. Also add a server-side buffer so we never flush unless we have a complete JSON object or a heartbeat interval elapsed. Patch includes tests and a config:```json
{
  "streaming": {
    "max_partial_flush_ms": 5000,
    "heartbeat_interval_ms": 1000
  }
}
```

dinesh (SRE): I will prepare a KB snippet for customers using: nginx, envoy, gRPC-web gateways. Example for nginx: ```nginx
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_request_buffering off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
add_header X-Accel-Buffering "no";
```

henry (SDK): On SDK side, shipping a patch that buffers by default until it sees the SSE `

` delimiter or a max buffer length. Also adding a `resume_token` header to reconnect requests so server can dedupe. PR incoming.

marie (Support): Olga — want to try the canary? We can enable heartbeat for your tenant and have you test with your gateway.

olga (Customer): yes please. enable the canary and I'll run the same curl trace and report back in 15 min. Thank you. :pray:

deploy-bot: rolling canary flag streaming.heartbeat.enable for tenant AcmeHealth -> edge-pool-3 (3/3 healthy).

marie (Support): billing-bot, can we tentatively grant a credit equal to estimated duplicate tokens for that window?

billing-bot: provisional credit created against tenant AcmeHealth: 1200 tokens. Final adjustment pending root cause.

olga (Customer): quick follow up: their corporate proxy is a gRPC-web gateway that rewrites to HTTP/1.1 and adds a `Content-Length` header when it sees small chunks. I suspect that's what caused this.

kai (Eng-runtime): noted. we'll treat headers that rewrite `Transfer-Encoding` as suspect and force server-side heartbeat + buffer for that tenant until they fix the gateway. Also plan: add server header `X-Redwood-Stream-State: partial` so operators can identify streams that got coalesced.

dinesh (SRE): Follow-ups: - create a postmortem note in incidents with root cause and KB link - test plan for various proxies - automated detection alert when we see >0.5% streams with partial chunk signs.

marie (Support): I'll keep this thread updated. thanks everyone.

olga (Customer): Verified: with heartbeat enabled reconnects decreased, partial events gone in my curl test. thanks.

marie (Support): closing loop: action items assigned to eng-runtime (kai), eng-sre (dinesh), sdk (henry), billing. We'll publish KB and schedule a follow-up QA run in 48h. :white_check_mark:
